newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian farm minister says crops better this year.
newsitem.headline: Russian farm minister says crops better this year.

text.p: Russian crops are in much better shape this year, Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun said on Friday.
"The condition of crops this year is significantly better compared to last year, and the first results of the harvest are encouraging," Interfax news agency quoted him as saying.

Khlystun adhered to his forecast of 1997 net grain output of at least 70 million tonnes, saying production would rise since use of mineral fertilisers had increased 10 percent. Greater inputs had protected plantings against a parasite known as the bedbug-turtle, which usually destroys some crops.
But Khlystun cautioned that a lack of fuel to get harvestors out to fields could result in what he termed gigantic losses. The ministry had said previously losses could be 12 million tonnes.
Russia needs 35-37 trillion roubles (around $6 billion) to bring in the harvest.

First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Thursday output would be 80 million tonnes. Last year's grain harvest was 69.3 million tonnes, the second poor result in a row and one of the top-three worst in 30 years.
